A cube-shaped sugar cube is dissolving uniformly in tea. If the surface area of the cube is decreasing at a rate of $24\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\text{/s},$ at what rate are the edges changing when each edge is $2\,\text{cm}?$ Assume that each edge is decreasing at the same rate, and the rate of decrease of the edge is positive.

The cube's edge is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
$\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the side of the cube, let $S$ be its surface area, and let $V$ be its volume. All of the variables change with time. In particular, we are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=-24\,{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$

We want to find the rate of change of $x$ knowing the rate of change of $S.$ So, we start with the formula for the surface area of the cube:

$$
S=6{x}^{2}
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(S) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =12x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug in the known values into the above expression. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =12x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ -24 & =12(2)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the edges are decreasing at a rate of $1\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
